thread:
alex: Quick question — when can we skip a semver bump for docs-only PRs? Releasebot suggested a patch for a README change and it's noisy.

pm_kate: Generally docs-only shouldn't force a public bump. We keep churn down. Releasebot heuristics look at paths and sometimes over-eagerly suggest a patch.

sam: Agreed. Our lightweight rule: if no code/runtime/API change, mark as docs-only. Use `meta: docs-only` in the PR body and add `skip-release` label to avoid bumping.

deploy-bot: releasebot detected changed files: [docs/**/*.md, website/**], suggested bump: patch. To override, add label `skip-release` or a comment `/no-bump`.

jen: Can we standardize on a single override label? People keep using different ones (`no-bump`, `skip-release`, `docs`). I'd prefer `skip-release`.

lia: Also call out edgecases: docs + ci config changes — if config affects runtime (e.g., dockerfile/entrypoint), treat as code. If it's just CI docs or badges, it's safe to skip.

sam: For customer-impacting hotfixes the flow is different: label `hotfix`, bump patch, pin to the dedicated channel, and do a canary rollout (10%) with 30m observation. Rollback = revert + redeploy that tag. We don't try to reuse a semver number.

alex: How should we record docs-only activity so PMs/ops aren't blind if we intentionally skip a bump?

pm_kate: Add an entry in the internal changelog under a "Docs (no-bump)" heading. Also leave a one-line note in the release console / changelog UI so audits can find it.

jen: Example PR body snippet we should add to the PR template: 
```
meta: docs-only
release-notes: skip
labels: [skip-release]
```

sam: Nice — I'll update the playbook with explicit labels and the exact command (`/no-bump` vs label) so releasebot behavior is deterministic.

lia: :thumbsup: Also adding a small checklist: "Does this touch runtime?" helps reviewers avoid mistakes.

alex: Thanks. If you post the updated snippet here I'll copy it into the template now.

pm_kate: Pasting now — will also link the playbook when PR merged.
